public_rationale: OpenAI announced $122 billion in committed capital on March 31, 2026; this does not establish future financing sufficiency or cash available to meet obligations [e1]. Anthropic's May 28 financing disclosure included $15 billion in previously committed investments, rather than a measurement of unrestricted cash [e2]. Its April 20 announcement scheduled capacity additions through 2026 without establishing completion of the contemplated buildout [e3]. These disclosures establish neither company's complete forecast conditions or a subsequent liquidity failure, and they do not demonstrate durable ability to meet obligations under those conditions [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: OpenAI's calendar 2028 revenue outcome is not established by these 2026 disclosures.
Financing commitments are not measurements of cash received or available liquidity.
Anthropic's full capacity commissioning and associated payment obligations are not established.
The forecast gives no cash-exhaustion deadline; the two companies have different conditions.

our_interpretation: Treat the two companies as separate conditional branches. OpenAI requires both the revenue shortfall and insufficient financing; Anthropic requires the referenced capacity to be built and the stated monthly revenue shortfall.
For OpenAI, the context supplies a reported $113 billion revenue projection for calendar 2028, alongside approximate monthly figures. That revenue year is not a deadline for cash exhaustion.
Run out of money means insufficient available liquidity to meet obligations when due.
The cash outcome has no stated accounting basis. The contextual revenue projection is a press estimate and cannot supply an accounting basis for cash.
criteria.support_condition: After the respective antecedent is established, reliable liquidity and obligation records show that the company cannot meet payments because available funds are exhausted.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the respective antecedent is established, records demonstrate a durable ability to meet obligations without the revenue or financing the claim treats as necessary. Continued operation for a short interval is insufficient.

evidence.explanation: OpenAI disclosed substantial financing commitments before the post. This neither proves cash receipt nor establishes whether financing will be insufficient when the future revenue condition can be assessed.
Anthropic's round includes previously committed financing. These commitments cannot be treated as realized revenue or a measurement of unrestricted cash.
The announcement describes staged future capacity additions. It does not establish completion of all capacity contemplated by Zitron or when its full payment obligations become due.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Assess each branch separately. Establish OpenAI's 2028 revenue shortfall and insufficient financing, or Anthropic's completed referenced buildout and stated monthly revenue shortfall. Then obtain dated liquidity and obligation records showing either inability to meet payments from exhausted funds or durable ability to meet them despite the applicable conditions.
